**Wire verb `stats fit-mixed`**: Fit one linear mixed model per feature of a feature-by-sample table, with a random intercept per group of samples (dataset, donor, day), and test each named coefficient with a Wald t.

# Wraps

- [`MixedModel.Fit`](https://github.com/smith-chem-wisc/mzLib/blob/d10017ce/mzLib/StatisticalModels/MixedModel.cs) in `mzLib/StatisticalModels/MixedModel.cs` at mzLib `d10017ce`
- [`MixedModelFit`](https://github.com/smith-chem-wisc/mzLib/blob/d10017ce/mzLib/StatisticalModels/MixedModel.cs) in `mzLib/StatisticalModels/MixedModel.cs` at mzLib `d10017ce`
- [`VarianceEstimator`](https://github.com/smith-chem-wisc/mzLib/blob/d10017ce/mzLib/StatisticalModels/MixedModel.cs) in `mzLib/StatisticalModels/MixedModel.cs` at mzLib `d10017ce`
- [`FeatureFitStatus`](https://github.com/smith-chem-wisc/mzLib/blob/d10017ce/mzLib/StatisticalModels/LinearModel.cs) in `mzLib/StatisticalModels/LinearModel.cs` at mzLib `d10017ce`

# Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Unit | Range | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `responses` (wire `--responses`) | `path` | required | — | — | stats fit's responses table. A TSV with a header row: the first column is the feature id (unique, any header) and every other column is one sample, named by its header. Cells are used as given, so log-transform intensities first. A blank cell, NA or NaN (any case) is missing and is omitted from that feature's fit, never imputed. A 0 is an OBSERVATION. Blank lines are skipped. |
| `design` (wire `--design`) | `path` | required | — | — | stats fit's design table: a TSV with a header row and one row per sample, the sample name (matching the responses header exactly, rows matched by name) then one column per fixed-effect coefficient, every cell a finite number. Include an intercept column if you want one; do not add a column per group, which the random intercept replaces. mzLib refuses a design that is not of full column rank over all samples. |
| `groups` (wire `--groups`) | `path` | required | — | — | A TSV with a header row and one row per sample: the sample name, then EXACTLY ONE column, the sample's group label (a dataset accession, a donor, an acquisition day), whose header names the grouping. The sample names must be exactly the responses' sample columns, in any order. Labels are text, trimmed and compared exactly; NA is a label like any other. An empty label is refused by mzLib (MixedModel.Fit), naming the sample. |
| `stdin` (wire `--stdin`) | `string[]` | required | — | `>= 1 line; each a design column name, none repeated` | The coefficients to report, one design column name per line. The model always fits every design column; the table holds one block of rows per coefficient named here, in this order. |
| `estimator` (wire `--estimator`) | `string` | absent | — | `reml \| ml` | How the variances are estimated: reml is mzLib's VarianceEstimator.Reml (restricted maximum likelihood, not biased downward by the number of coefficients), ml is VarianceEstimator.MaximumLikelihood (biased variances in small samples, but log-likelihoods comparable between designs). Absent, the bridge sends none and MixedModel.Fit's default applies (Reml at d10017ce); the envelope's estimator says which was used. |
| `threads` (wire `--threads`) | `int` | `1` | threads | `>= 1, or -1 for every core` | Features fitted at once. The bridge default is 1 (BULK.md); mzLib's own default is -1. Results are identical at any value (mzLib). |

# Returns

Top-level fields:

| Field | Type | Unit | Null? | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `responses_file` | `string` | — | never | Absolute path of the responses table. |
| `design_file` | `string` | — | never | Absolute path of the design table. |
| `groups_file` | `string` | — | never | Absolute path of the groups table. |
| `grouping` | `string` | — | never | The groups file's label column header. |
| `group_names` | `string[]` | — | never | The distinct labels, in order of first appearance over the responses' samples (the order mzLib numbers them in). |
| `group_count` | `int` | groups | never | Distinct labels over all samples. A feature's own count, over its observed samples, is its groups column. |
| `feature_count` | `int` | features | never | Feature rows read. |
| `sample_count` | `int` | samples | never | Sample columns read. |
| `sample_names` | `string[]` | — | never | In responses header order, which is the order the design and group rows were put in. |
| `coefficient_names` | `string[]` | — | never | Every design column, in order. |
| `tested_coefficients` | `string[]` | — | never | The stdin coefficients, in order; the table holds one block of feature\_count rows per entry. |
| `estimator` | `string` | — | never | reml or ml: the estimator mzLib reports it fitted with (MixedModelFit.Estimator), the default when --estimator was absent. |
| `threads` | `int` | threads | never | The thread count used. |
| `missing_count` | `int` | cells | never | Response cells that were blank, NA or NaN. |
| `zero_count` | `int` | cells | never | Response cells that are exactly 0, fitted as observations. |
| `status_counts` | `map<string,int>` | features | never | Features per status, always these six keys: fitted, too\_few\_observations, rank\_deficient, too\_few\_groups, variance\_ratio\_at\_limit, not\_converged. They are the outcomes MixedModel.Fit's body can return at d10017ce; a stop-gap until mzLib says per model (mzLib\#1487). |
| `row_count` | `int` | rows | never | feature\_count x the number of tested coefficients. |
| `columns` (wire `column_names`) | `string[]` | — | never | The table's columns, in order. |
| `columns` | `table` | — | never | One row per (tested coefficient, feature): coefficient blocks in stdin order, features in file order. |
| `caveats` | `string[]` | — | never | Seven static caveats (one of them says which estimator), plus one each, with counts, when any feature was not fitted, when a fitted row has no df, when a fitted feature's group\_variance is 0, and when any cell is 0. |

Per-row fields (one value per record, in `columns` or each list entry):

| Field | Type | Unit | Null? | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `feature` | `string` | — | never | The feature id from the responses file's first column. |
| `coefficient` | `string` | — | never | The coefficient this row reports. |
| `status` | `string` | — | never | fitted \| too\_few\_observations (no more observed samples than coefficients) \| rank\_deficient (the design restricted to the observed samples is not of full rank) \| too\_few\_groups (fewer than two observed groups, or no group observed twice, so group and residual variance cannot be told apart) \| variance\_ratio\_at\_limit (group\_variance / residual\_variance ran to the top of mzLib's search, e^12, typically near-identical replicates within each group) \| not\_converged (the likelihood at the chosen variance ratio could not be evaluated: a non-finite value, or a residual sum of squares of 0 or below). Only fitted rows carry statistics. |
| `estimate` | `float` | response units per coefficient unit (e.g. log2 fold change for a 0/1 column on log2 intensities) | yes: status is not fitted | The generalized-least-squares fixed-effect coefficient at the estimated variances: the effect within groups, each group keeping its own baseline. |
| `standard_error` | `float` | response units per coefficient unit | yes: not fitted | sqrt of the diagonal of s^2 (X' V^-1 X)^-1 with s^2 = RSS / (observed - coefficients), under both estimators, as nlme's summary reports. |
| `df` | `float` | degrees of freedom | yes: not fitted, or the containment df is not positive (a group-level coefficient with too few observed groups to test it) | Denominator df of the t test, by nlme's containment rule for one grouping level, a whole number: observed - observed groups - within-group coefficients for a coefficient that varies within some group and for the intercept; observed groups - group-level coefficients, minus 1 more with an intercept, for one constant within every group. |
| `t` | `float` | standard errors | yes: not fitted | Wald statistic, estimate / standard\_error. Reported even when df is null. |
| `p_value` | `float` | fraction (0 to 1) | yes: not fitted, or df is null | Two-sided p-value of the t test on df. Not adjusted across features. |
| `residual_variance` | `float` | squared response units | yes: not fitted | sigma^2, the within-group variance: RSS / (observed - coefficients) under reml, RSS / observed under ml. The same in every coefficient block. |
| `group_variance` | `float` | squared response units | yes: not fitted | tau^2, the between-group variance of the random intercept. 0 is the boundary estimate (no between-group variance), which nlme cannot reach and reports as a tiny positive value. The same in every coefficient block. |
| `log_likelihood` | `float` | log-likelihood (natural log) | yes: not fitted | The maximized log-likelihood, restricted under reml. The same in every coefficient block. |
| `observed` | `int` | samples | never | Samples with a finite response for this feature. |
| `groups` | `int` | groups | never | Distinct groups among this feature's observed samples. |

# Errors

| Kind | mzLibRust returns | When |
|---|---|---|
| `usage` | [`MzLibError::Usage`](crate::MzLibError::Usage) | responses, design or groups missing, blank or not found; a table empty, header-only or with too few columns; the groups file with other than two columns or an empty label header; a row whose field count differs from its header; an empty or repeated feature id, sample or coefficient name; a response cell that is not a number (other than blank, NA, NaN); a design cell that is not a finite number |
| `usage` | [`MzLibError::Usage`](crate::MzLibError::Usage) | the design's or the groups' samples are not exactly the responses' sample columns (both differences are named); no coefficient on stdin, one named twice, or one not in the design; --estimator other than reml or ml, or without a value; --threads 0 or below -1 |
| `usage` | [`MzLibError::Usage`](crate::MzLibError::Usage) | mzLib refuses the input (its ArgumentException, reclassified): a design not of full column rank; a sample whose group label is empty, named by 0-based position and then by its name |
| `correctness` | [`MzLibError::Bridge`](crate::MzLibError::Bridge) | never expected |
| `service_unavailable` | [`MzLibError::ServiceUnavailable`](crate::MzLibError::ServiceUnavailable) | never returned by this verb |

Any call can also fail on the way to mzLib or back, whatever the verb: [`MzLibError::BridgeNotFound`](crate::MzLibError::BridgeNotFound), [`MzLibError::Timeout`](crate::MzLibError::Timeout), [`MzLibError::Protocol`](crate::MzLibError::Protocol) or [`MzLibError::Io`](crate::MzLibError::Io).

# Caveats

- A random intercept per group and nothing more, as nlme::lme(y ~ ..., random = ~ 1 \| group): no random slopes, nested or crossed groupings, or residual correlation.
- Fixed effects are tested by Wald t on nlme's containment degrees of freedom. Satterthwaite and Kenward-Roger (lmerTest, pbkrtest) are not implemented, so p-values differ from lmerTest's. mzLib matches nlme 3.1.169 to 1e-5 relative (nlme's own optimizer precision) in estimates, standard errors, variances, p-values and log-likelihoods, with identical df.
- group\_variance 0 is the boundary estimate. nlme works on the log scale, cannot reach 0, and reports a tiny positive value there instead.
- Under reml, log\_likelihood is the restricted log-likelihood: compare it only between models with the same fixed effects, and use --estimator ml to compare designs. Under ml, residual\_variance is RSS / observed, but standard errors use RSS / (observed - coefficients), as nlme's summary reports ML fits.
- p\_value is not adjusted across features. Send one coefficient's p\_value column to stats adjust for Benjamini-Hochberg.
- A 0 is an observation. Log-transform intensities first, and blank any cell that means 'not measured'.
- A feature the fixed effects fit exactly (a constant one, say) is reported fitted, with a residual\_variance at rounding level (about 1e-16) and a meaningless t and p\_value: MixedModel's not\_converged guard catches only a residual sum of squares of exactly 0 (d10017ce). Check residual\_variance before trusting a very small p\_value. Pinned by StatisticsTests.FitMixed\_AnExactFit\_IsReportedFitted\_WithRoundingLevelVariance.
